processing: An organic garden whose documented output includes green tea alongside the orthodox processing usual for Darjeeling black tea, which is withered, rolled, oxidised and dried.
harvest_season: As across Darjeeling, first flush in spring and second flush from around May to June, followed by monsoon and autumn pickings.
appearance_dry: Twisted leaf in mixed olive and brown for black lots; greener in green tea.
appearance_liquor: Gold to amber for black lots, paler for green.
appearance_wet: Mixed green and coppery leaf in black lots.
taste_profile: Few tasting records name this garden. Black lots should follow the Darjeeling pattern, floral in spring and fruitier in summer.

brewing.notes: Brewed Western-style. For a green lot, use water around 80 C and a shorter steep.

vintage_note: As usual for Darjeeling, expect it sold by year and flush, with green and black lots named separately. Buy the latest harvest and check which type you are getting.
description:
Monteviot is an 88-hectare organic garden in the Kurseong valley, on slopes from 950 to 1,700 metres. It belongs to the same organic group as Ambootia, Happy Valley and Sivitar.

Green tea is the output recorded for it, which is unusual enough in Darjeeling to be worth checking on the label. Other lots, if you meet them, are likely to be black made in the usual orthodox way.

For a black lot, expect the regional pattern and brew as for other Darjeeling. For a green lot, cool the water well down, or it turns harsh.

Little is recorded about how it reaches buyers, so buy small and ask which year and flush you are getting.
history:
Monteviot was established in 1856, which puts it among the older Darjeeling gardens. In 2004 its factory burnt down completely.

Today it is listed under Darjeeling Organic Tea Estates Private Ltd. Little else about its past is well documented.
